question: Should OpenClaw adopt this shared localization platform and its Gateway, plugin/skill metadata, and operator-surface contract as the intended core product direction for the foundation series?
rationale: The branch introduces a cross-cutting product and compatibility contract; source review can assess implementation shape, but cannot decide whether this permanent core/API surface is the desired product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the RFC direction
options.body: Approve the shared contract, then require scoped current-head proof and compatibility coverage before landing the implementation slices.

options.title: Narrow the core boundary
options.body: Keep only the smallest shared locale primitives in core and route presentation-specific metadata or optional integrations through existing owner/plugin seams.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Defer the platform until maintainers define supported locales, ownership, and public compatibility guarantees.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the RFC direction
recommendation.body: Approve the shared contract, then require scoped current-head proof and compatibility coverage before landing the implementation slices.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor authored the RFC-linked series and is the clearest available contact for clarifying the proposed architecture; final acceptance should include the relevant code-area owners.
